title: ElasticityFit
description: One fitted price elasticity for one variant. Written by Lane C into `elasticity_fits`, read by Lane B's forecast endpoint. One row per (shop, variant, model_version); the freshest row wins.

elasticity.description: Own-price elasticity, normally negative: -1.6 means a 1% price rise gives 1.6% fewer units. Positive values are permitted but Lane B demotes confidence to `assumption` and warns.

se.description: Standard error of `elasticity` (bootstrap). Used for the fitted range's width when `low`/`high` are absent. null only if the method genuinely cannot produce one.

low.description: Lower credible bound on the elasticity itself (nominal `interval`, default 80%). Supply this when the posterior is asymmetric — a symmetric `elasticity ± z·se` would misstate the range the forecast card shows. Must be <= `high`.

high.description: Upper credible bound on the elasticity itself. Send `low` and `high` together or not at all; when both are present the forecast uses them verbatim instead of deriving an interval from `se`.

interval.description: Nominal coverage of [low, high]. Defaults to 0.8 when omitted.

price_variation_pct.description: Spread of observed prices in the fitting window, as a percent of the mean price. The single best predictor of whether this fit is trustworthy.

confidence.description: Lane C's honest self-assessment by data richness. `assumption` means 'do not lean on this' — Lane B will serve bracket math instead.

confidence_explanation.description: Optional one-liner in plain language, e.g. 'this price has never changed, so we used a store-wide average'.

method.description: Free-form, e.g. 'loglog_ridge_eb_shrunk'. For debugging and model cards, never rendered to merchants.

shrinkage_weight.description: 0 = the estimate is entirely the portfolio prior, 1 = entirely this variant's own data.

model_version.description: Matches model_runs.model_version (R31) — every number is traceable to the run that made it.
